ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line AB and CD intersect at point O, $ \angle DOE = 90^\circ$, OD bisects $ \angle BOF$, $ \angle BOE = 50^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $ \angle EOF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OD$ bisects $\angle BOF$, \\
$\therefore \angle DOF=\angle BOD=40^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle EOF=\angle DOF+\angle DOE=40^\circ+90^\circ=\boxed{130^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, multiple rays emanate from point O; CD is a horizontal straight line passing through O, with D on the right side and C on the left side; AB is an oblique line passing through O, with B in the upper right and A in the lower left; OE is vertically upward, and OF is obliquely downward to the right. In the figure, a right-angle mark is drawn between OE and OD, and ray OB is located inside the right angle formed by OE and OD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠DOE = 90°, and ∠BOE = 50°. Because OB is inside ∠DOE, ∠BOD = ∠DOE - ∠BOE = 90° - 50° = 40°. Also because OD bisects ∠BOF, ∠DOF = ∠BOD = 40°. The required ∠EOF is composed of the adjacent ∠EOD and ∠DOF, therefore ∠EOF = 90° + 40° = 130°.
